companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce (核心本地商业) segment operating profit/(loss)
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's disclosed Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/loss. The segment bundles food delivery, Instashopping and in-store/hotel/travel, and it absorbs almost all of Meituan's delivery-war subsidy cost. Meituan does not break out a delivery-only loss. Q3 2026 results are not out yet; they are due around late November, in line with the Nov 28 release last year.

Meituan FY2025 results 2026-03-26 (Beijing News, Xinhua: Q4 core local commerce operating loss ~RMB10bn)

Meituan Q2 2026 results 2026-08-28 (163.com, qq.com, cls.cn; operating margin +7.9% vs -3.2% in Q1; +52.3% YoY vs RMB3.7bn)

companies.latest_signal: Core Local Commerce swung to a RMB5.67bn operating profit in Q2 2026, its first profit after three loss-making quarters. Chinese coverage (Tencent News, 163, CLS) puts this down to the subsidy war cooling after the June 2026 regulatory crackdown, and Meituan says it still holds more than 60% of delivery GTV. Treat the Q2 profit as a high base: the Q3 print, due soon, will test whether it holds as Alibaba and JD keep spending.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Taobao Shangou (Flash Sale)/Ele.me instant-retail EBITA loss (analyst estimate; no company-disclosed figure)
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba discloses no standalone instant-commerce P&L. It reports only instant-retail revenue and qualitative language: 'losses continue to narrow' and 'unit economics improving q/q'. The figures below are sell-side estimates (CICC, Guosen, Huayuan) quoted in Chinese financial press. They are not company disclosures.

Aug 20, 2026 results disclosed only that Flash Sale unit economics improved q/q, driven by higher order value and fulfilment efficiency. No loss figure, and instant-retail revenue was RMB53.3bn, up 45%.
Zhitong Finance/10jqka preview, Nov 18, 2026; company said on Nov 19 only that 'losses continued to narrow'

companies.latest_signal: On Nov 19, 2026, Alibaba said instant-retail revenue rose 22% YoY to RMB58.8bn, driven mainly by Hema. It said Flash Sale market share is stable, losses are still narrowing, and unit economics keep improving q/q. Management is shifting Flash Sale targets from order volume to order value and profit quality. The trend is clearly down from the Q3 2025 peak of about RMB37bn, but the exact loss is unconfirmed, and the decline from roughly RMB18bn to roughly RMB9bn over the last three quarters is estimate-based.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_name: New Businesses (新业务) segment operating loss
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed New Businesses segment operating loss. It covers JD Takeaway (food delivery), Jingxi, JD Property and overseas. JD does not disclose a standalone food-delivery loss. In Q3 2026, instant delivery was moved into JD Logistics, which cut segment revenue and may flatter the comparison.

JD Q3 2026 results, 2026-11-18 (The Paper, Sina Tech, Eastmoney, 21jingji): -38.7% YoY, with segment revenue down 50% to RMB7.8bn

companies.latest_signal: JD said Q3 food-delivery loss narrowed more than 50% YoY and kept narrowing q/q, helped by better subsidy efficiency, better delivery efficiency and higher commission and ad revenue. Orders and users both rose q/q. The segment loss improved only about RMB0.2bn q/q (9.85 to 9.64), so the pace of narrowing has stalled. JD gave no breakeven date and only targets a 'significant' further YoY reduction in 2027.

war_summary: The war has cooled sharply from its Q3 2025 peak. Meituan is back in operating profit at Core Local Commerce, Alibaba's Flash Sale loss is down roughly 75% from peak on analyst estimates, and JD's New Businesses loss is down about 39% YoY. Chinese coverage (CLS, Huxiu, 21jingji) credits SAMR's draft ten-point rules on delivery-platform subsidies and the 'anti-involution' push, with estimates of RMB150-173bn burned industry-wide (HSBC puts it at RMB173bn: Alibaba 87bn, Meituan 44bn, JD 42bn). Nobody has formally blinked: Meituan kept more than 60% share and Alibaba still targets unit-economics breakeven by FY2027 and EBITA breakeven around FY2029. The sequential improvement at JD has nearly stopped, and Alibaba still carries roughly RMB9bn a quarter of losses. The main risk is a re-escalation if Meituan's Q3 print shows the profit rebound is holding while the other two are still losing money. Caveats: Alibaba's numbers are sell-side estimates, JD's Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 figures and Meituan's Q1 2026 figure were not re-verified in this session, and I could not open LatePost directly, so the sources are Chinese-language press (Sina, 163, Tencent News, Eastmoney, The Paper, 21jingji, Huxiu, Zhitong).
